summary: The exact candidate fixes PR 2799's three named MI355X regressions and passes isolated GPU numerical/remapping tests, but independent boundary cases still select a slower compact path and the hard pre-dedup gate discards a highly overlapping, memory-beneficial union. Target NVIDIA BF16 FlashMLA output and end-to-end performance remain unverified.

tests.what_was_measured: The recorded base uses unconditional full-prefix dequantization and has no selective helper; the import fails from the checkout source path.
Four GPU tests passed against checked-out source: independent FP8 numerical reference, physical alias dedup/remap, fallback behavior, pre-dedup gate, and invalid sentinels.
The inherited 64/256/1024-query cases all took early full fallback with a 150994944-byte peak and measured 0.890x/0.872x/0.875x of the separately warmed full baseline.
The beneficial 262144-row case remained selective: 4029 compact rows, 4641408 BF16 bytes versus 301989888, and 2.541x speedup.

Independent MI355X medians around the gate: random 1/4/8/16/24/32-query compact cases were 1.011x/1.020x/1.060x/1.210x/1.327x/1.347x full latency. A 33-query highly overlapping input fell back to 150994944 bytes although forcing dedup produced 2048 rows at 4930048-byte peak and 0.993x latency.
One subtest passed and four skipped; flashmla_sparse and flashmla_kv stopped before attention because page size 64 is unsupported by the available legacy HIP DSA path, which requires page size 1.

gpu_evidence: Exact-candidate unit, numerical, memory, and timing checks executed checked-out Python/Triton source on one AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950) with Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 and a fresh private Triton cache.
remaining_counterexamples: At 131072 prefix rows and top-k 2048, random 1 through 32 query-row inputs select compact staging but were 1.011x to 1.347x slower than warmed full dequantization on the assigned MI355X.

At 131072 prefix rows, 33 query rows, and top-k 2048 with complete cross-query overlap, the entry-count gate falls back to the 150994944-byte full buffer; forcing the union yields 2048 compact rows at 4930048-byte peak with essentially equal latency.
BF16 flashmla_sparse attention output correctness and end-to-end sparse-prefill performance remain unverified on the required NVIDIA Hopper/Blackwell architecture.
remaining_limitations: The assigned AMD Instinct MI355X is not NVIDIA Hopper/Blackwell and cannot execute the target FlashMLA sparse attention kernel.
The ROCm integration fixture stops before attention because page size 64 is incompatible with the available legacy HIP DSA path's page-size-1 requirement.
The candidate's fixed thresholds are validated only with isolated staging microbenchmarks on MI355X, not end-to-end or on the target architecture.
No native source changed, so a native rebuild was not applicable; only the changed checkout-source Python/Triton path was freshly compiled and executed.
